draft.title: What a logarithm is
card: log_a(x) is the power that a must be raised to, to give x. The number a is called the base.
Example: 2³ = 8, so log₂ 8 = 3. Read it as: 2 to what power gives 8? The answer is 3.
To work one out, ask the question in words. For log₃ 81, ask: 3 to what power gives 81? Since 3⁴ = 81, log₃ 81 = 4.
Logarithms undo exponentials. The statements a^y = x and log_a(x) = y say the same thing, so you can swap between the two forms.
draft.remember: A logarithm is a power: log_a(x) asks what power of a gives x.

a.q: What is the value of log₅ 25?
a.why: 5² = 25, so 5 must be raised to the power 2. The answer 5 is tempting because it is the base, but the logarithm is the power, not the base.

b.q: Which exponential statement is the same as log₄ x = 3?
b.why: log₄ x = 3 means 4 raised to the power 3 gives x, so 4³ = x. The option 3⁴ = x swaps the base and the power, which is a common mistake.
b.clue: The base of the logarithm stays the base of the power.
